It does not function as a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, fragrance component, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal.","category":"Botanical plant extract / antioxidant"}

camellia sinensis leaf extract__skincare.analysis: {"name":"Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Camellia sinensis leaf extract is a plant-derived ingredient rich in polyphenols and antioxidants that can help soothe and protect the skin. It is generally well tolerated and considered safe for most skin types.","details":"This extract, commonly known as green tea extract, may offer anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidative benefits, helping to reduce redness and protect against environmental stressors. It is not related to parabens, sulfates, phthalates, formaldehyde-releasing preservatives, fragrance, mineral oil, silicones, drying alcohols, or heavy metals in typical cosmetic use. Mild irritation or allergy is possible but uncommon, usually in individuals with specific plant sensitivities.","category":"Botanical extract / antioxidant"}

rosmarinus officinalis (rosemary) leaf e.analysis: {"name":"Rosmarinus Officinalis (rosemary) Leaf Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Rosemary leaf extract is a botanical ingredient often used for its antioxidant and mild antimicrobial properties. It is generally safe but can occasionally irritate very sensitive or allergy-prone skin.","details":"This extract may help protect the formula and the skin from oxidative damage and can provide mild astringent and purifying effects. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, synthetic fragrance, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal. Some individuals sensitive to rosemary or fragrant plant extracts may experience irritation or allergic reactions, but this is relatively uncommon at typical usage levels.","category":"Botanical extract / antioxidant"}

centella asiatica extract__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Centella Asiatica Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Centella Asiatica Extract is a plant extract known for its soothing and skin-repairing properties. It is widely used in skincare for sensitive or irritated skin.","details":"Rich in compounds like asiaticoside and madecassoside, it can help support skin barrier function, calm redness, and promote the appearance of smoother, healthier skin. It is not associated with major safety concerns such as endocrine disruption or carcinogenicity, and it is not part of paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing, or heavy metal groups. Mild irritation or allergy is possible in very sensitive individuals, as with any botanical ingredient.","category":"Botanical extract / soothing agent"}

betaine__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Betaine","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Betaine is a hydrating and soothing ingredient commonly used in skincare and haircare products. It is generally well-tolerated and not associated with major safety concerns.","details":"Betaine is a naturally derived osmolyte that helps skin and hair maintain moisture balance and improve softness, making it useful in cleansers, moisturizers, and conditioners. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, fragrance, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal, and it has a low potential for irritation or sensitization in most users. Its safety profile is considered favorable for regular use, including in sensitive-skin formulations.","category":"Humectant and moisturizing agent"}

allantoin__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Allantoin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Allantoin is a soothing and skin-conditioning ingredient known for supporting skin barrier repair and reducing irritation. It is considered safe and gentle for most skin types, including sensitive skin.","details":"Allantoin is used to promote skin comfort by helping to calm redness and support the natural healing process, making it common in moisturizers, after-sun products, and products for irritated or dry skin. It is not linked to endocrine disruption, does not belong to parabens, sulfates, phthalates, formaldehyde-releasing preservatives, fragrances, mineral oils, silicones, drying alcohols, or heavy metals. Adverse reactions are rare, and it is widely regarded as a low-risk ingredient in cosmetic formulations.","category":"Soothing and skin-conditioning agent"}

trehalose__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Trehalose","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Trehalose is a sugar-based humectant that helps retain moisture and protect skin from dehydration. It is generally considered safe and non-irritating in cosmetic use.","details":"Trehalose can help stabilize formulations and protect skin cells against environmental stress by binding water and improving hydration, which is beneficial in moisturizers, serums, and haircare products. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, fragrance, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal, and it has a low risk of sensitization or irritation. Its use is broadly accepted in skincare, including for sensitive and dry skin types.","category":"Humectant and moisturizing agent"}

polyglyceryl-3 methylglucose distearate_.analysis: {"name":"Polyglyceryl-3 Methylglucose Distearate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Polyglyceryl-3 Methylglucose Distearate is an emulsifier derived from plant oils and sugars, used to blend oil and water in skincare. It is generally considered gentle and well tolerated by most skin types.","details":"This ingredient helps stabilize creams and lotions and can contribute to a smooth, non-greasy texture. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, fragrance, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal. Adverse reactions are rare and usually limited to individuals with very sensitive or allergy-prone skin.","category":"Emulsifier / surfactant"}

isopropyl myristate__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Isopropyl Myristate","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Isopropyl Myristate is an emollient that makes products feel silky and helps spreadability. It is generally safe but can be comedogenic, meaning it may clog pores and worsen acne in some people.","details":"In skincare, it softens the skin and enhances the penetration of other ingredients, improving sensory feel. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, fragrance, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal, but it can be problematic for oily or acne-prone skin due to its tendency to contribute to breakouts. People with sensitive, acne-prone, or easily congested skin may prefer lower concentrations or to patch test first.","category":"Emollient / texture enhancer"}

peg-100 stearate__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Peg-100 Stearate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"PEG-100 Stearate is an emulsifier that helps oil and water mix in creams and lotions. It is widely used and generally considered safe for topical use in cosmetics.","details":"This ingredient stabilizes formulations and contributes to a smooth, creamy texture without significant risk of irritation for most users. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, fragrance, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal, though PEG-type ingredients can sometimes be of concern if contaminated during manufacturing; reputable brands control for this. People with very sensitive or compromised skin may still wish to patch test new products containing PEGs.","category":"Emulsifier / surfactant"}

sodium polyacrylate__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Sodium Polyacrylate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Sodium Polyacrylate is a synthetic polymer used as a thickener, absorbent, and film-forming agent in skincare and haircare products. It is generally considered low risk for most users.","details":"This ingredient helps stabilize formulas and improve texture by absorbing water and increasing viscosity. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde releaser, fragrance, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal. Rarely, it may cause mild irritation in very sensitive or compromised skin, mainly if present in high concentrations or in poorly formulated products.","category":"Polymer / Rheology modifier"}

2-hexanediol__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"2-hexanediol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"2-Hexanediol is a synthetic diol used mainly as a solvent and humectant, and sometimes as a mild preservative booster in cosmetic formulas. It is generally considered low risk with a good safety profile at typical use levels.","details":"It helps dissolve other ingredients and can provide light moisturizing properties while supporting the preservation system. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, fragrance, mineral oil, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal. Some people with very sensitive skin may experience mild irritation, but this is uncommon at standard cosmetic concentrations.","category":"Solvent / Humectant / Preservative booster"}

caprylyl glycol__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Caprylyl Glycol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Caprylyl Glycol is a humectant and skin-conditioning agent that also functions as a preservative booster. It is widely used in skincare and haircare and is generally considered low risk.","details":"This ingredient helps attract and retain moisture in the skin while enhancing the effectiveness of preservatives, allowing for lower levels of stronger antimicrobial agents. It does not belong to the main concerning groups such as parabens, sulfates, phthalates, formaldehyde releasers, fragrance allergens, mineral oil, silicones, drying alcohols, or heavy metals. Mild irritation can occur in very sensitive individuals, but adverse reactions are relatively rare.","category":"Humectant / Skin conditioning agent / Preservative booster"}

beeswax__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Beeswax","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Beeswax is a natural wax produced by honeybees, commonly used as an occlusive and thickening agent in skincare. It is generally safe and well-tolerated, helping to protect and moisturize the skin.","details":"Beeswax forms a protective barrier on the skin that helps reduce transepidermal water loss without being highly comedogenic for most people. It is not linked to parabens, sulfates, phthalates, formaldehyde-releasing preservatives, or heavy metals. Individuals with known bee or pollen allergies may rarely experience sensitivity or allergic reactions and should patch test first.","category":"Natural wax / Occlusive / Thickener"}

cetyl ethylhexanoate__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Cetyl Ethylhexanoate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cetyl ethylhexanoate is an ester used as a lightweight emollient and texture enhancer in skincare and haircare products. It is generally considered safe with a low irritation potential for most users.","details":"This ingredient provides a smooth, non-greasy feel and helps spreadability, often serving as an alternative to heavier oils or silicones. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, or drying alcohol, and it is not associated with heavy metals. Very sensitive or acne-prone skin may occasionally experience mild comedogenicity or irritation, but this is uncommon.","category":"Emollient ester / Texture enhancer"}

butylene glycol__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Butylene Glycol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Butylene glycol is a commonly used humectant and solvent that helps keep skincare products stable and skin hydrated. It is generally considered low risk and well tolerated by most skin types.","details":"In skincare, butylene glycol attracts and holds water in the skin and improves the texture and spreadability of formulations. It has a low irritation and sensitization potential, though very sensitive or reactive skin may occasionally experience mild redness or stinging. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde releaser, or heavy metal and is not associated with hormone disruption.","category":"Humectant / Solvent"}

macadamia ternifolia seed oil__skincare_.analysis: {"name":"Macadamia Ternifolia Seed Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Macadamia ternifolia seed oil is a plant-derived emollient oil rich in fatty acids that helps moisturize and soften skin and hair. It is generally considered safe with a low risk of irritation.","details":"This oil contains monounsaturated fatty acids such as oleic and palmitoleic acid, which support skin barrier function and provide a smooth, conditioned feel. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, or mineral oil, and it does not act like silicones or drying alcohols. People with nut allergies should patch test first, as there is a theoretical risk of sensitivity due to its nut origin.","category":"Plant oil / Emollient"}

cyclopentasiloxane__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Cyclopentasiloxane","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cyclopentasiloxane is a volatile silicone that gives skincare and haircare products a silky slip and lightweight feel. It is generally low risk for most users, with rare irritation or allergy reports.","details":"This ingredient evaporates after application, helping spread other ingredients evenly and leaving a smooth, non-greasy finish. While some people prefer to avoid silicones due to buildup concerns in hair or personal preference, cyclopentasiloxane itself is not known to be a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde releaser, or heavy metal. It can occasionally cause issues for very sensitive or acne-prone skin, so patch testing is advisable if you are reactive to silicones.","category":"Silicone / Texture enhancer"}

hamamelis virginiana (witch hazel) extra.analysis: {"name":"Hamamelis Virginiana (witch Hazel) Extract","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Witch hazel extract is a plant-derived astringent used to reduce oiliness, tighten pores, and soothe skin. It is generally safe but can be irritating or drying, especially if high in alcohol or used on sensitive or compromised skin.","details":"Hamamelis Virginiana (Witch Hazel) Extract contains tannins and other polyphenols that provide anti-inflammatory and mildly antioxidant effects, making it common in toners and acne-prone skin formulas. However, many commercial witch hazel extracts are distilled with ethanol, which can increase dryness, irritation, and disruption of the skin barrier, particularly for dry, sensitive, rosacea-prone, or eczema-prone skin. While it is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releaser, mineral oil, silicone, or heavy metal, its astringency and possible alcohol content place it in a moderate risk category for irritation with frequent or high-concentration use.","category":"Botanical extract / astringent"}

dimethiconol__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Dimethiconol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Dimethiconol is a silicone polymer used to create a smooth, silky feel and to form a protective film on skin or hair. It is considered low risk for most users and is not a common allergen.","details":"This ingredient helps improve spreadability, reduce friction, and provide conditioning benefits, especially in haircare and skincare products. It is generally non-irritating and non-sensitizing, and it is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde releaser, or heavy metal. The main concern is that, as with other silicones, it can temporarily occlude the skin or hair surface, which may feel heavy to some users or potentially contribute to buildup if not cleansed properly.","category":"Silicone / Emollient"}

polysorbate 20__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Polysorbate 20","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Polysorbate 20 is a non-ionic surfactant and emulsifier used to help mix oil and water and improve product texture. It is generally considered low risk in skincare at typical use levels.","details":"Polysorbate 20 is derived from sorbitol and fatty acids and is widely used to solubilize essential oils and fragrances in water-based formulas. The main concern is potential trace impurities from its manufacturing process, but these are strictly controlled in cosmetics and not usually an issue for most users. It can occasionally cause mild irritation in very sensitive skin but is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde releaser, silicone, mineral oil, or drying alcohol.","category":"Emulsifier / Solubilizer / Surfactant"}

polyglutamic acid__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Polyglutamic Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Polyglutamic Acid is a humectant and film-forming polymer that helps attract and retain moisture in the skin. It is considered low risk and is often used for hydrating and plumping benefits.","details":"This ingredient is typically produced by fermentation and can increase skin hydration by forming a lightweight, flexible film on the surface of the skin. It is generally non-irritating and compatible with most skin types, including sensitive skin. It is not associated with parabens, sulfates, phthalates, formaldehyde-releasing preservatives, fragrance, mineral oil, silicones, drying alcohols, or heavy metals.","category":"Humectant / Hydrating polymer"}

glycyrrhiza glabra (licorice) root extra.analysis: {"name":"Glycyrrhiza Glabra (licorice) Root Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Licorice root extract is a plant-derived ingredient used for skin brightening, soothing, and antioxidant benefits. It is generally well tolerated but can rarely cause irritation or allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.","details":"In skincare, licorice root extract helps reduce the appearance of dark spots and uneven tone by inhibiting melanin production, and it also provides anti-inflammatory properties that can calm redness and irritation. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, fragrance, mineral oil, petrolatum, silicone, drying alcohol, or heavy metal. Adverse effects are uncommon, but people with very sensitive or allergy-prone skin should patch test first, as botanical extracts can occasionally trigger contact dermatitis.","category":"Botanical extract / skin brightening and soothing agent"}

xylitol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Xylitol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Xylitol is a sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener in many food products. It is generally considered safe for human consumption and may benefit dental health.","details":"Xylitol provides sweetness with fewer calories than sugar and has a minimal effect on blood glucose, making it popular in sugar-free gum, candies, and diabetic-friendly foods. In some people, especially at higher intakes, it can cause digestive discomfort such as gas, bloating, or diarrhea due to its laxative effect. It is extremely toxic to dogs, so products containing xylitol should be kept away from pets.","category":"Sweetener / Sugar alcohol"}

ceramide np__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Ceramide Np","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Ceramide NP is a lipid ingredient primarily used in cosmetics and skincare, not commonly used in food products. When present in a food-related context, it is usually associated with topical or cosmetic applications rather than ingestion.","details":"Ceramide NP helps restore and support the skin barrier and is widely recognized as safe for topical use. There is limited data on its use as an ingested food ingredient, but typical consumer exposure is through skin-contact products rather than diet. If it appears on a label of a food-related product, it is most likely part of a cosmetic or personal-care item rather than an edible component.","category":"Cosmetic lipid / Skin conditioning agent"}

cyclohexasiloxane__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cyclohexasiloxane","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Cyclohexasiloxane is a synthetic silicone compound used mainly in cosmetics and personal care products, not approved or intended as a food ingredient. Its presence in a food product would be considered inappropriate and potentially unsafe.","details":"This ingredient is designed for topical use (such as in skin and hair products) to provide a smooth, silky texture and evaporates from the skin after application. It is not recognized as a food additive and has not been evaluated as safe for ingestion in the way food ingredients are. Finding cyclohexasiloxane in a food product label suggests mislabeling or contamination and should be treated as a serious concern.","category":"Non-food cosmetic silicone"}

stearic acid__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Stearic Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Stearic acid is a common saturated fatty acid found naturally in animal fats and some vegetable oils and is used in foods as an emulsifier, stabilizer, or anti-caking agent. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) when used in normal food quantities.","details":"In food products, stearic acid can help improve texture, prevent ingredients from clumping, and aid in the processing of chocolates, candies, and supplements. Although it is a saturated fat, stearic acid is considered metabolically neutral compared with some other saturated fats, and typical dietary levels are not associated with major health risks. People on very low-fat diets or with specific medical advice to limit saturated fats may still want to monitor overall intake.","category":"Fatty acid / food additive"}

shea butter (butyrospermum parkii)__food.analysis: {"name":"Shea Butter (butyrospermum Parkii)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Shea butter is a natural fat extracted from the nuts of the shea tree and is sometimes used in food as an edible fat. It is generally recognized as safe for consumption when used in appropriate amounts.","details":"Shea butter is rich in fatty acids and is more commonly used in cosmetics, but food-grade shea butter can be used similarly to other vegetable fats. People with tree nut allergies may rarely react, but such reactions to shea are considered uncommon. It does not contribute artificial additives, colors, or preservatives.","category":"Natural fat / oil"}

anise fruit extract (illicium verum)__fo.analysis: {"name":"Anise Fruit Extract (illicium Verum)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Anise fruit extract is a natural flavoring derived from the fruit of Illicium verum, commonly used to provide a licorice-like taste in foods. It is generally safe when used in normal food flavoring amounts.","details":"This extract contains aromatic compounds (such as anethole) that give a sweet, spicy flavor to baked goods, candies, and beverages. Some sensitive individuals may experience mild digestive or allergic reactions, but this is uncommon at typical dietary levels. It does not function as an artificial color, preservative, or sweetener.","category":"Natural flavoring"}

disodium edta__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Disodium Edta","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Disodium EDTA is a synthetic chelating agent used in foods to bind metal ions and improve stability and shelf life. It is approved for use in limited amounts but is a purely artificial additive.","details":"In foods, disodium EDTA helps prevent discoloration, rancidity, and loss of flavor by binding trace metals such as iron and copper. Regulatory agencies set strict maximum levels because high doses in animals have been linked to mineral depletion and other effects, though typical dietary exposure in humans is much lower. For people aiming to minimize artificial additives and preservatives, this ingredient is one to limit where possible.","category":"Preservative / chelating agent"}

glyceryl stearate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Glyceryl Stearate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Glyceryl stearate is an ester of glycerin and stearic acid that can be used as an emulsifier in foods and is generally recognized as safe. It is more commonly used in cosmetics than in foods.","details":"In food applications, glyceryl stearate helps blend water and oils and can improve texture, especially in processed or baked goods. It is not associated with major toxicity or allergenicity at typical dietary exposure levels. For most consumers, it does not pose significant health concerns when consumed in normal amounts.","category":"Food emulsifier / processing aid"}

hamamelis virginiana (witch hazel) extra.analysis: {"name":"Hamamelis Virginiana (witch Hazel) Extract","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Witch hazel extract is derived from the Hamamelis virginiana plant and is primarily used topically in cosmetics, not as a common food ingredient. Its safety profile for ingestion is less established, and preparations may contain alcohol or tannins that could irritate the gastrointestinal tract in some people.","details":"When consumed, witch hazel preparations can contain tannins that may cause stomach upset or interact with certain medications if taken in significant amounts. There is limited data on chronic oral exposure in typical food-use scenarios, so its risk as a food ingredient is less clearly defined compared with standard food additives. People with sensitivities to botanical extracts or with liver or kidney conditions should be cautious about ingesting products containing witch hazel extract.","category":"Botanical extract / atypical food ingredient"}

dimethiconol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Dimethiconol","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Dimethiconol is a silicone polymer widely used in cosmetics and personal care products, not as a conventional food ingredient. Its safety has been studied mainly for topical use, and it is not an approved or typical food additive in many jurisdictions.","details":"As a high–molecular weight silicone, dimethiconol is considered inert on the skin, but there is very limited safety data for oral consumption in foods. Use of non-food-grade silicones in food could pose unknown or unnecessary risk, especially with long-term ingestion. Because it falls outside normal, well-characterized food additive categories, its presence in a food product should be treated cautiously and verified for regulatory compliance.","category":"Non-food silicone polymer / cosmetic ingredient"}

camellia sinensis leaf extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Camellia sinensis leaf extract is derived from the tea plant and is commonly used for its antioxidant properties. It is generally considered safe in food products at typical consumption levels.","details":"This extract contains polyphenols such as catechins, which may provide health benefits including antioxidant and potential cardiovascular support. In foods, it is usually present in small amounts and is not associated with major allergens or common food additive concerns. Sensitive individuals who are reactive to caffeine or tea compounds should be aware that some extracts can contain small amounts of caffeine.","category":"Plant extract / natural antioxidant"}

rosmarinus officinalis (rosemary) leaf e.analysis: {"name":"Rosmarinus Officinalis (rosemary) Leaf Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Rosemary leaf extract is a natural extract used mainly as a flavoring and antioxidant in foods. It is generally recognized as safe for most people when used in typical food quantities.","details":"This extract contains compounds such as rosmarinic acid and carnosic acid that help protect fats and oils from oxidation, extending shelf life. It may contribute a mild herbal flavor and can be used as a more natural alternative to synthetic preservatives. Rarely, people with herb allergies or sensitivities may react to rosemary, but such cases are uncommon at typical food-use levels.","category":"Herbal extract / natural antioxidant"}

centella asiatica extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Centella Asiatica Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Centella asiatica extract comes from a medicinal herb (also known as gotu kola) and is sometimes added to foods or supplements for its potential health benefits. It is generally considered safe at typical food or supplement doses.","details":"The extract contains triterpenoids that have been studied for potential effects on circulation, skin health, and cognition, though evidence in food-level doses is limited. It is not a common allergen and does not belong to major food allergen groups like gluten, dairy, soy, or nuts. Very high supplemental doses may cause digestive upset in some individuals, but such levels are unlikely in ordinary food products.","category":"Herbal extract / botanical ingredient"}

chamomilla recutita (matricaria) flower.analysis: {"name":"Chamomilla Recutita (matricaria) Flower Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Chamomile flower extract is a plant-derived ingredient commonly used for its soothing and antioxidant properties. In food or beverages, it is generally considered safe for most people.","details":"Chamomile is often consumed as herbal tea and used as a natural flavor or botanical extract, and it does not involve artificial additives, colors, or sweeteners. The main concern is for individuals with allergies to plants in the Asteraceae/Compositae family (such as ragweed), who may experience allergic reactions. It does not contribute to trans fats, high sodium, or common food additive risks.","category":"Herbal extract / botanical ingredient"}

scutellaria baicalensis root extract__fo.analysis: {"name":"Scutellaria Baicalensis Root Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Scutellaria baicalensis (Chinese skullcap) root extract is a herbal ingredient rich in flavonoids and used for its antioxidant and traditional medicinal properties. In small amounts in foods or supplements, it is generally considered low risk for most healthy adults.","details":"This root extract is a natural botanical and is not associated with artificial colors, sweeteners, flavor enhancers, or common food additives. Some reports suggest that very high supplemental doses may stress the liver in susceptible individuals, so people with liver disease or those taking multiple medications should use caution and consult a professional. It does not contribute to trans fats, high sodium, or common allergen exposure such as gluten, dairy, soy, or nuts.","category":"Herbal extract / botanical ingredient"}

polygonum cuspidatum root extract__food_.analysis: {"name":"Polygonum Cuspidatum Root Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Polygonum cuspidatum root extract (also known as Japanese knotweed extract) is a natural source of resveratrol and other polyphenols. It is widely used in dietary supplements and occasionally in functional foods for its antioxidant properties.","details":"As a botanical extract, it generally poses low risk when used in typical food or supplement doses and is not related to artificial sweeteners, colors, preservatives, or flavor enhancers. Mild digestive upset may occur at high supplemental intakes, and people on multiple medications should be cautious because resveratrol can theoretically interact with some drug-metabolizing enzymes. It is not a common allergen and does not add significant sodium, trans fats, or hydrogenated oils to foods.","category":"Herbal extract / botanical ingredient"}

betaine__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Betaine","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Betaine is a naturally occurring compound found in foods like beets, whole grains, and spinach, and is sometimes added to foods or supplements. It is generally recognized as safe at typical dietary levels.","details":"In food products, betaine may be present naturally or added for its role in supporting methylation and cellular hydration. Most people tolerate it well, though very high supplemental doses can occasionally cause digestive upset in sensitive individuals. It is not associated with common food allergies, artificial colors, or major additive concerns.","category":"Nutrient/functional ingredient"}

allantoin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Allantoin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Allantoin is a compound often used in cosmetics for skin-soothing purposes and may rarely appear in specialty food or oral-care products. At low levels, it is considered safe and not a major dietary risk factor.","details":"When present in products that can be ingested, allantoin is typically used in very small quantities and has a low toxicity profile. It is not known to contribute to common food-related issues such as high sodium, artificial sweeteners, trans fats, or major allergen exposure. Adverse reactions are uncommon and usually limited to rare individual sensitivities.","category":"Functional ingredient"}

trehalose__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Trehalose","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Trehalose is a naturally occurring sugar used as a sweetener and stabilizer in foods. It has a similar caloric value to other sugars and is generally recognized as safe for most people.","details":"In food products, trehalose can improve texture and shelf life and provide mild sweetness without being an artificial sweetener. It does contribute carbohydrates and calories, so excessive intake may impact blood sugar in people with diabetes or those managing carbohydrate intake. It is not a common allergen and is distinct from high fructose corn syrup and artificial flavor enhancers.","category":"Carbohydrate sweetener / stabilizer"}

butylene glycol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Butylene Glycol","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Butylene glycol is a synthetic solvent and humectant more commonly used in cosmetics than in foods. In food, it may function similarly to other glycols as a carrier or texturizer when used.","details":"Data on butylene glycol as a food ingredient are limited compared with better-studied glycols like propylene glycol, so its long-term safety profile in foods is less well characterized. It can cause irritation or intolerance in sensitive individuals at higher exposures, particularly when used on skin, and by analogy with related glycols may cause digestive upset if consumed in large amounts. Its presence in a food-type product may also suggest the item could be intended for cosmetic or topical use rather than regular consumption.","category":"Solvent and humectant"}

macadamia ternifolia seed oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Macadamia Ternifolia Seed Oil","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Macadamia ternifolia seed oil is a plant-derived oil rich in fats, including monounsaturated fatty acids. For most people it is safe, but it is a tree nut–derived ingredient and therefore a potential allergen.","details":"People with macadamia nut or broader tree nut allergies should avoid products containing this oil, as even refined oils can sometimes trigger reactions. Nutritionally, macadamia oil is high in calories and fat, so large intakes can contribute to excess energy consumption, but in typical food amounts it is generally well tolerated in non-allergic individuals. In many products it is also used topically (cosmetics), so its presence in a ‘food’ product should be interpreted with care.","category":"Tree nut oil (allergen)"}

cyclopentasiloxane__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cyclopentasiloxane","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Cyclopentasiloxane is a volatile silicone compound used in cosmetics and personal care products, not approved as a conventional food ingredient. Its presence indicates the product is likely intended for external use rather than eating.","details":"Regulatory and safety assessments for cyclopentasiloxane focus on topical exposure, not ingestion, and it is not recognized as a safe food additive. Consuming products containing this silicone could pose unknown or unnecessary risks, and accidental ingestion should be minimized, especially in children. From a food safety perspective, this ingredient is inappropriate in products meant for regular consumption.","category":"Silicone (cosmetic-grade, non-food additive)"}

polysorbate 20__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Polysorbate 20","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Polysorbate 20 is an emulsifier and surfactant used to mix oil and water in food and cosmetic products. It is generally recognized as safe in small amounts but may cause sensitivity or digestive upset in some individuals.","details":"As a synthetic additive derived from sorbitol and fatty acids, Polysorbate 20 helps stabilize mixtures, improve texture, and extend shelf life in certain processed foods. Regulatory agencies usually consider it safe within approved limits, but very high or chronic intakes of emulsifiers have been questioned in research for potential effects on gut health, and some people may experience mild allergic or irritant reactions. Its presence typically indicates a processed product rather than a minimally processed food.","category":"Emulsifier / food additive"}

polyglutamic acid__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Polyglutamic Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Polyglutamic acid is a polymer of the amino acid glutamic acid, often produced by fermentation and mainly used in supplements or cosmetic products rather than common foods. When used in food-related applications, it is generally considered low risk at typical intake levels.","details":"In food contexts, polyglutamic acid may appear as a fermentation-derived ingredient that can influence texture or moisture retention, and it is related to naturally occurring compounds found in fermented soy foods like natto. Current evidence does not show significant toxicity at amounts used in foods or supplements, though data in large populations is still limited. People with known sensitivities to glutamate-containing products should monitor tolerance, but for most consumers it is unlikely to pose health concerns at normal dietary exposure.","category":"Amino acid-derived ingredient / texturizer"}

glycyrrhiza glabra (licorice) root extra.analysis: {"name":"Glycyrrhiza Glabra (licorice) Root Extract","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Glycyrrhiza glabra (licorice) root extract is a herbal ingredient that can add sweetness and flavor and may have medicinal effects. In higher doses or with frequent use, it can affect blood pressure, potassium levels, and certain medications.","details":"Licorice root naturally contains glycyrrhizin, which can lead to sodium retention, potassium loss, elevated blood pressure, and fluid retention if consumed in significant amounts over time. This makes it a concern for people with hypertension, heart or kidney disease, during pregnancy, or for those taking certain medications such as diuretics or blood pressure drugs. Small amounts used occasionally in flavored foods are usually well tolerated, but regular or high intake warrants caution and medical advice if underlying health conditions exist.","category":"Herbal extract / flavoring"}

cetearyl alcohol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cetearyl Alcohol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cetearyl alcohol is a fatty alcohol used primarily as an emulsifier and stabilizer, and it is uncommon in conventional food products. It is generally considered low risk when ingested in small amounts, but its use is far more typical in cosmetics than foods.","details":"Unlike simple alcohols such as ethanol, cetearyl alcohol is a mixture of cetyl and stearyl fatty alcohols that are waxy and have low toxicity. Regulatory authorities typically regard fatty alcohols as safe at low levels, but data on frequent oral exposure in foods are more limited because they are far more common in topical products. People with very sensitive digestive systems may experience mild discomfort at high doses, but this is unlikely at typical incidental intake levels.","category":"Emulsifier / stabilizer (uncommon in foods, common in cosmetics)"}

beeswax__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Beeswax","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Beeswax is a natural wax produced by honeybees and is used in foods mainly as a glazing agent, coating, or release agent. It is generally recognized as safe for human consumption in the small quantities normally used in food products.","details":"In foods, beeswax helps provide a protective coating (for example on fruits, candies, or supplements) and is minimally absorbed or metabolized. Allergic reactions are rare but can occur in people with strong bee or bee-product allergies, so those individuals should exercise caution. It does not contribute significant calories, sodium, or sugars and is not associated with common food additive concerns such as artificial colors, preservatives, or flavor enhancers.","category":"Natural glazing agent / coating"}

cetyl ethylhexanoate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cetyl Ethylhexanoate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cetyl ethylhexanoate is an ester used mainly in cosmetics as an emollient and texture enhancer, and it is not a typical food ingredient. Any incidental oral exposure from products is expected to be low risk, but it is not intended to be a regular dietary component.","details":"Toxicological data suggest low acute toxicity and it functions as an inert, oily compound, but its safety evaluations are focused on skin contact rather than long-term ingestion. Because it is not used to modify flavor, color, or preservation, it does not carry the usual food additive concerns (such as MSG, artificial colors, or artificial sweeteners). Regular or intentional consumption is not recommended due to the lack of extensive food-use data.","category":"Emollient / texture agent (primarily cosmetic, not standard food additive)"}

glycerin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Glycerin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Glycerin (glycerol) is a sugar alcohol used as a humectant, sweetener, and texture enhancer in foods. It is generally recognized as safe for most people when consumed in normal food amounts.","details":"Glycerin helps retain moisture, adds slight sweetness, and improves smoothness in various food products. High intakes may cause digestive discomfort such as gas or diarrhea in sensitive individuals, but it is not associated with major long-term health risks at typical dietary levels.","category":"Humectant / sweetener"}

olive fruit oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Olive Fruit Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Olive fruit oil (from Olea europaea) is a natural edible oil rich in monounsaturated fats and bioactive compounds. It is widely considered a heart-healthy fat when used in place of saturated or trans fats.","details":"In foods, olive oil contributes flavor, healthy fats, and antioxidants such as polyphenols and vitamin E. Most people tolerate it well, though individuals with olive or latex-related allergies should be cautious; overall it is a safer alternative to hydrogenated oils and trans fats.","category":"Edible oil / fat"}

sodium polyacrylate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sodium Polyacrylate","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Sodium polyacrylate is a superabsorbent polymer widely used in diapers and cosmetics, not typically approved as a direct food ingredient. Its presence in food would be unconventional and potentially raise safety and regulatory concerns.","details":"If ingested in small incidental amounts (for example from packaging), it is generally considered to have low acute toxicity, but it is not evaluated or intended as a regular dietary component. There may be risks of gastrointestinal irritation or impurities from production if consumed in significant quantities. In the context of food, this ingredient should be questioned and verified against local food safety regulations.","category":"Non-food polymer / processing aid or packaging-related substance"}

2-hexanediol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"2-hexanediol","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"2-Hexanediol is primarily used in cosmetics and industrial applications as a solvent and preservative component, not as a standard food additive. Its intentional use directly in food is unusual and may not be covered by typical food safety approvals.","details":"Toxicological data suggest relatively low acute toxicity at small doses, but there is limited safety data for chronic oral intake in humans. Because it is not a common food additive and may not be approved as such in many jurisdictions, its presence in a food product should be carefully reviewed with regulatory guidelines. Until confirmed otherwise, it should be treated with caution in the context of regular dietary exposure.","category":"Solvent / preservative-type compound (non-standard food additive)"}

caprylyl glycol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Caprylyl Glycol","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Caprylyl glycol is commonly used in cosmetics as a humectant and preservative booster, and it is not a widely recognized direct food additive. Its deliberate inclusion in foods is atypical and may fall outside standard food additive approvals.","details":"Available data indicate low acute toxicity and relatively good safety in topical cosmetic use, but oral safety data for long-term, repeated ingestion are limited. In food, any use should be evaluated against local food regulations and acceptable daily intake data, if available. Until its regulatory status and safety for ingestion are clearly established, it should be considered a cautious or questionable ingredient in food products.","category":"Humectant / preservative booster (primarily cosmetic-use ingredient)"}

polyglyceryl-3 methylglucose distearate_.analysis: {"name":"Polyglyceryl-3 Methylglucose Distearate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Polyglyceryl-3 methylglucose distearate is an emulsifier typically used in cosmetics and sometimes in specialty food applications. It is generally considered to have low toxicity when ingested in small quantities.","details":"This ingredient is formed from polyglycerin, methylglucose, and stearic acid and helps mix oil- and water-based components. There is limited data on its use in foods, but structurally related polyglyceryl emulsifiers are widely regarded as safe in normal dietary amounts. People with very sensitive digestion may prefer to limit highly processed emulsifiers, but no major health risks are documented at typical food-use levels.","category":"Emulsifier / texture agent"}

isopropyl myristate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Isopropyl Myristate","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Isopropyl myristate is an oil-like ester commonly used in cosmetics and topical products, and it is not typically intended for use in foods. Ingestion in non-trivial amounts may cause gastrointestinal irritation or discomfort.","details":"While small incidental amounts are unlikely to be highly toxic, this substance is primarily evaluated for dermal rather than dietary exposure. Its presence in a food product is unusual and suggests the product may be cosmetic or non-food, or that labeling is atypical. Because of limited safety data for regular oral consumption, it is prudent to consider it a higher concern than standard food-grade fats and to avoid frequent intake.","category":"Non-food cosmetic-grade emollient / ester"}

peg-100 stearate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Peg-100 Stearate","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"PEG-100 stearate is a polyethylene glycol–based emulsifier widely used in cosmetics and sometimes as a processing aid, but it is not a common food-grade ingredient. Concerns center on potential impurities (like ethylene oxide or 1,4-dioxane) and limited data on chronic oral intake.","details":"PEG-containing compounds are generally of low acute toxicity, but they are synthetic and can carry trace manufacturing by-products if not highly purified. PEG-100 stearate is intended mainly for external use, and its routine consumption in foods is not well studied. For regular dietary use, it is safer to favor emulsifiers with established food-grade approvals and long-term ingestion data.","category":"Synthetic emulsifier / surfactant"}

extracto de raíz de scutellaria baicalen.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Raíz de Scutellaria Baicalensis","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Extracto botánico con propiedades antioxidantes y calmantes para la piel. Generalmente se considera un ingrediente seguro y bien tolerado en cosmética.","details":"La raíz de Scutellaria baicalensis es rica en flavonoides como la baicalina, que pueden ayudar a proteger la piel del daño oxidativo y a reducir el enrojecimiento. No está asociado a parabenos, sulfatos, ftalatos, liberadores de formaldehído, fragancias sintéticas, aceites minerales, siliconas, alcoholes secantes ni metales pesados. Las reacciones adversas son poco frecuentes y suelen limitarse a posibles alergias individuales a extractos vegetales.","category":"Extracto vegetal / antioxidante"}

cera de abejas__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Cera de Abejas","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La cera de abejas es un emoliente natural que ayuda a formar una barrera protectora sobre la piel, reduciendo la pérdida de humedad. Generalmente es bien tolerada y considerada segura en cosméticos.","details":"La cera de abejas se utiliza en productos para el cuidado de la piel y el cabello por sus propiedades oclusivas y suavizantes, mejorando la textura y la hidratación. No está relacionada con parabenos, sulfatos, ftalatos, liberadores de formaldehído ni fragancias sintéticas. El principal riesgo es para personas con alergia específica a productos derivados de las abejas, que podrían experimentar irritación o reacción alérgica.","category":"Emoliente y agente filmógeno natural"}

manteca de butyrospermum parkii (karité).analysis: {"name":"Manteca de Butyrospermum Parkii (karité)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La manteca de karité es un emoliente natural muy nutritivo que ayuda a hidratar y suavizar la piel. Generalmente es bien tolerada y se considera segura en cosmética.","details":"Aporta lípidos y ácidos grasos que refuerzan la barrera cutánea, reduciendo la sequedad y la descamación. Puede contener trazas de proteínas de la nuez de karité, por lo que en personas extremadamente sensibles a frutos secos podría existir un leve riesgo de irritación o alergia. No está relacionada con parabenos, sulfatos, ftalatos, formaldehído, fragancias sintéticas ni metales pesados.","category":"Emoliente y agente hidratante de origen vegetal"}

extracto de hoja de romero (rosmarinus o.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Hoja de Romero (rosmarinus Officinalis)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Extracto vegetal con propiedades antioxidantes y antimicrobianas, generalmente bien tolerado en productos para el cuidado de la piel y el cabello.","details":"El extracto de hoja de romero se utiliza para ayudar a proteger la fórmula y la piel del daño oxidativo, además de aportar un leve efecto purificante y tonificante. Puede causar irritación o alergia de contacto en personas muy sensibles a los aceites esenciales o a las plantas de la familia Lamiaceae, pero en las concentraciones cosméticas habituales su perfil de seguridad se considera bueno. No está asociado a parabenos, sulfatos, ftalatos, liberadores de formaldehído, fragancia sintética, aceites minerales, siliconas, alcoholes secantes ni metales pesados.","category":"Extracto botánico / antioxidante"}

extracto de raíz de polygonum cuspidatum.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Raíz de Polygonum Cuspidatum","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Extracto vegetal rico en resveratrol con propiedades antioxidantes y calmantes para la piel. Generalmente se considera seguro en productos cosméticos.","details":"Se utiliza en el cuidado de la piel por su contenido en polifenoles, que ayudan a proteger frente al daño oxidativo y a apoyar la función de barrera cutánea. Suele tener buena tolerancia, aunque en pieles muy sensibles puede causar irritación leve o enrojecimiento de forma poco frecuente. No está asociado a disruptores hormonales, sulfatos, ftalatos, liberadores de formaldehído ni fragancias sintéticas.","category":"Extracto botánico antioxidante"}

xilitol__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Xilitol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El xilitol es un alcohol de azúcar utilizado como humectante y agente hidratante en productos para el cuidado de la piel. Ayuda a mantener la humedad cutánea y es considerado seguro para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"En cosmética, el xilitol mejora la hidratación de la piel al ayudar a retener agua en la capa córnea y puede contribuir a reforzar la barrera cutánea. Generalmente tiene bajo potencial irritante y alérgico, aunque en pieles extremadamente sensibles podría causar ligera irritación en casos aislados. No está relacionado con parabenos, sulfatos, ftalatos, liberadores de formaldehído, fragancias, aceites minerales, siliconas, alcoholes secantes ni metales pesados.","category":"Humectante e hidratante"}

glicol caprílico__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Glicol Caprílico","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El glicol caprílico es un humectante y emoliente que ayuda a mantener la piel hidratada y suave. También posee ligeras propiedades antimicrobianas que ayudan a conservar la fórmula.","details":"Este ingrediente derivado de ácidos grasos se utiliza con frecuencia en productos para el cuidado de la piel y el cabello por su buena tolerancia y baja probabilidad de irritación en la mayoría de las personas. Ayuda a mejorar la textura del producto y a reducir la pérdida de agua transepidérmica. En pieles muy sensibles o comprometidas puede producir una leve irritación, pero los reportes son poco frecuentes.","category":"Humectante y emoliente"}

extracto de raíz de regaliz (glycyrrhiza.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Raíz de Regaliz (glycyrrhiza Glabra)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Ingrediente vegetal con propiedades calmantes e iluminadoras de la piel, útil para reducir manchas y enrojecimiento. Generalmente se considera seguro en cosmética tópica.","details":"El extracto de raíz de regaliz es rico en compuestos como la glabridina, que ayuda a modular la producción de melanina y puede mejorar la apariencia de hiperpigmentaciones. También tiene propiedades antioxidantes y antiinflamatorias, por lo que es adecuado para pieles sensibles o con tendencia a irritarse. Las reacciones adversas suelen ser raras y se limitan principalmente a posibles alergias o sensibilidades individuales.","category":"Extracto botánico / activo calmante e iluminador"}

ciclopentasiloxano__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Ciclopentasiloxano","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El ciclopentasiloxano es una silicona volátil que se usa para aportar una textura sedosa y facilitar la aplicación de productos para la piel y el cabello. Generalmente se considera de bajo riesgo para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"Este ingrediente forma una película ligera que suaviza la superficie de la piel y el cabello sin dejar sensación pegajosa, y suele evaporarse parcialmente tras la aplicación. En pieles muy sensibles o con tendencia al acné puede contribuir a la oclusión si se combina con otros ingredientes pesados, aunque por sí solo es poco irritante. Existen algunas preocupaciones ambientales sobre la acumulación de ciertas siliconas en el medio acuático, pero a nivel de salud humana tópica se considera seguro en concentraciones habituales.","category":"Silicona volátil / agente emoliente"}

ciclohexasiloxano__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Ciclohexasiloxano","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"El ciclohexasiloxano es un tipo de silicona volátil que se utiliza para aportar una textura sedosa y de fácil extensión en productos para la piel y el cabello. extracto de flor de manzanilla (chamomil.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Flor de Manzanilla (chamomilla Recutita/matricaria)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Extracto botánico calmante con propiedades antiinflamatorias y antioxidantes, muy usado en productos para piel sensible.","details":"La manzanilla puede ayudar a reducir enrojecimiento e irritación y aportar efecto suavizante a la piel. extracto de hoja de camellia sinensis (t.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Hoja de Camellia Sinensis (té Verde)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Extracto vegetal rico en antioxidantes que ayuda a proteger la piel del daño ambiental y a calmar la inflamación leve.","details":"El extracto de hoja de Camellia sinensis, conocido como té verde, contiene polifenoles y catequinas con propiedades antioxidantes y antiinflamatorias, útiles para cuidar pieles normales, mixtas y grasas. ácido poliglutámico__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Ácido Poliglutámico","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El ácido poliglutámico es un polímero derivado de aminoácidos con fuertes propiedades humectantes que ayuda a retener agua en la piel. extracto de centella asiática__skincare_.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Centella Asiática","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El extracto de Centella Asiática es un ingrediente botánico conocido por sus propiedades calmantes y reparadoras de la piel. betaína__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Betaína","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La betaína es un humectante y osmoprotector derivado comúnmente de la remolacha azucarera, utilizado para hidratar y suavizar la piel y el cabello. dimeticonol__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Dimeticonol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El dimeticonol es una silicona de alto peso molecular que forma una película suave sobre la piel y el cabello, mejorando la textura y la sensación al tacto. alantoína__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Alantoína","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La alantoína es un ingrediente calmante y reparador que ayuda a suavizar la piel y favorecer la regeneración de tejidos. peg-100 estearato__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Peg-100 Estearato","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El PEG-100 estearato es un tensioactivo y emulsionante sintético utilizado para mezclar agua y aceites en productos para el cuidado de la piel. poliacrilato de sodio__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Poliacrilato de Sodio","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El poliacrilato de sodio es un polímero sintético utilizado como agente espesante y absorbente en productos para el cuidado de la piel y el cabello. 2-hexanodiol__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"2-hexanodiol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El 2-Hexanodiol es un glicol utilizado como solvente y humectante en productos para el cuidado de la piel y el cabello. En pieles muy sensibles puede causar irritación leve o enrojecimiento si se usa en concentraciones altas o en combinación con otros activos irritantes.","category":"Solvente y humectante"}

trehalosa__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Trehalosa","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La trehalosa es un azúcar de origen natural que actúa como humectante y protector de la hidratación en la piel y el cabello. extracto de hamamelis virginiana (hamame.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Hamamelis Virginiana (hamamelis)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El extracto de hamamelis se utiliza como astringente y calmante en productos para el cuidado de la piel. butilenglicol__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Butilenglicol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El butilenglicol es un solvente y humectante que ayuda a mantener la hidratación de la piel y a mejorar la textura del producto. aceite de fruto de oliva (olea europaea).analysis: {"name":"Aceite de Fruto de Oliva (olea Europaea)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Aceite vegetal emoliente que ayuda a hidratar y suavizar la piel. polisorbato 20__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Polisorbato 20","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El polisorbato 20 es un tensioactivo y emulsionante derivado del sorbitol y del ácido láurico, usado para mezclar agua y aceites en productos cosméticos. disodium edta__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Disodium Edta","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Disodium EDTA es un agente quelante que se utiliza para estabilizar las fórmulas y mejorar la eficacia de conservantes en productos para el cuidado de la piel y el cabello. extracto de fruto de anís estrellado (il.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Fruto de Anís Estrellado (illicium Verum)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El extracto de fruto de anís estrellado se utiliza principalmente como ingrediente aromático y antioxidante en productos para el cuidado de la piel. miristato de isopropilo__skincare__es.analysis: {"name":"Miristato de Isopropilo","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"El miristato de isopropilo es un éster graso utilizado como emoliente y agente de textura en productos para el cuidado de la piel y el cabello. butyrospermum parkii (shea) butter__skin.analysis: {"name":"Butyrospermum Parkii (shea) Butter","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Shea butter is a natural plant butter used as a rich emollient and moisturizer in skincare. It has a low risk of irritation or sensitization, though people with very reactive skin or nut sensitivities should patch test. It is not linked to parabens, sulfates, phthalates, formaldehyde releasers, or heavy metals.","category":"Plant butter / Emollient"}

illicium verum (anise) fruit extract__sk.analysis: {"name":"Illicium Verum (anise) Fruit Extract","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Illicium verum (anise) fruit extract is a plant-derived ingredient often used for fragrance and potential antioxidant or soothing properties. It can pose a higher risk of irritation or sensitization compared with many non-fragrant plant extracts.","details":"Because this extract is typically used for its distinctive aroma, it functions partly as a fragrance component, and fragrant plant extracts can trigger irritation or allergic reactions, especially in sensitive or compromised skin. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, mineral oil, silicone, or drying alcohol, and it is not a known source of heavy metals. However, due to its fragrance-related potential, it is best used cautiously by those with reactive or eczema‑prone skin.","category":"Botanical extract / Fragrance component"}

cyclohexasiloxane__skincare__en.analysis: {"name":"Cyclohexasiloxane","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Cyclohexasiloxane is a volatile silicone used to give products a silky, spreadable texture and quick-drying feel. It is generally low-irritation for skin but raises environmental and potential bioaccumulation concerns.","details":"In skincare and haircare, cyclohexasiloxane functions primarily as an emollient and texture enhancer, helping products glide smoothly and evaporate without leaving a heavy residue. For most users, it has a low risk of irritation or sensitization and is considered non-comedogenic, though some people who avoid silicones for personal or acne-related reasons may wish to limit it. However, cyclic silicones (like cyclohexasiloxane and D4/D5 relatives) are under scrutiny for persistence and bioaccumulation in the environment, which contributes to a more cautious overall safety assessment.","category":"Silicone / Emollient"}

filtered water__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Filtered Water","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Filtered water is generally safe and is the main base in many beverages and foods.","details":"It serves primarily as a diluent or carrier for other ingredients and contributes no allergens, calories, or additives by itself. Health concerns are minimal when the water is properly treated and meets safety standards.","category":"Base ingredient"}

almonds__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Almonds","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Almonds are a nutritious nut but are a common tree nut allergen that can cause serious reactions in sensitive individuals.","details":"They provide healthy fats, protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals, which can be beneficial as part of a balanced diet. However, for people with tree nut allergies, even small amounts can trigger severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis.","category":"Tree nut allergen"}

tricalcium phosphate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Tricalcium Phosphate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Tricalcium phosphate is a calcium salt used as a mineral supplement and anti-caking or stabilizing agent in foods.","details":"It is generally recognized as safe in the amounts used in food products and can contribute to dietary calcium intake. Excessive intake from multiple fortified sources may be undesirable for people with certain kidney or mineral-balance issues, but typical food levels are not considered a significant risk.","category":"Mineral additive"}

dl-alpha tocopherol acetate (vitamin e).analysis: {"name":"Dl-alpha Tocopherol Acetate (vitamin E) (contains Almonds)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"DL-alpha tocopherol acetate is a synthetic form of vitamin E used as a nutrient supplement and antioxidant in foods. However, this product also contains almonds, which are a common tree nut allergen.","details":"Vitamin E (DL-alpha tocopherol acetate) is generally recognized as safe at typical food fortification levels and helps protect fats in foods from oxidation. Most people tolerate it well, though extremely high supplemental doses may pose health concerns, which are unlikely from normal food use. The presence of almonds is important for individuals with nut allergies, as even small amounts can trigger allergic reactions ranging from mild symptoms to severe anaphylaxis.","category":"Vitamin / antioxidant and tree nut allergen"}

vitamin a palmitate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Vitamin a Palmitate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Vitamin A palmitate is a synthetic, fat-soluble form of vitamin A used to fortify foods. It is generally safe at typical fortification levels but can be harmful in excessive doses.","details":"This compound combines vitamin A with palmitic acid to create a stable form suitable for use in processed foods like dairy products, cereals, and margarines. While normal dietary intake is considered safe and beneficial for vision, immunity, and skin health, chronic excessive intake may lead to vitamin A toxicity, particularly in pregnant individuals or those taking multiple vitamin A–containing supplements. People with specific health conditions affecting fat metabolism should discuss high supplemental intakes with a healthcare professional.","category":"Vitamin / nutrient fortifier"}

ergocalciferol (vitamin d2)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Ergocalciferol (vitamin D2)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Ergocalciferol, or vitamin D2, is a form of vitamin D used to fortify foods and supplements to support bone and immune health. It is generally safe at standard fortification levels but can be toxic in very high doses over time.","details":"Vitamin D2 is typically derived from plant or fungal sources and helps the body regulate calcium and phosphorus levels, supporting bone strength and muscle function. In fortified foods, the amounts used are well below toxicity thresholds for most people, though extremely high supplemental intakes can cause elevated blood calcium, kidney strain, and other health issues. Individuals with certain medical conditions or those taking high-dose vitamin D supplements should monitor total vitamin D intake with a healthcare provider.","category":"Vitamin / nutrient fortifier"}

sea salt__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sea Salt","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Sea salt is a common source of sodium used for flavor and preservation in foods. The main health concern is excessive sodium intake, which can contribute to high blood pressure and cardiovascular issues.","details":"Nutritionally, sea salt is very similar to regular table salt, with only trace amounts of additional minerals that usually do not provide significant health benefits. In typical processed foods, sea salt can contribute substantially to total daily sodium intake, especially when multiple salty products are consumed. Individuals with hypertension, kidney disease, or cardiovascular risk should monitor overall sodium intake regardless of the salt type used.","category":"Salt / Sodium"}

gellan gum__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Gellan Gum","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Gellan gum is a gelling and stabilizing agent produced by fermentation and widely used to improve texture in foods and beverages. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for most consumers at typical use levels.","details":"As a soluble fiber–like additive, gellan gum usually passes through the digestive tract without being absorbed and may occasionally cause mild gas or bloating in sensitive individuals at high intakes. Regulatory agencies such as the FDA and EFSA have evaluated it and found no significant toxicity or carcinogenic concerns at permitted levels. Suele considerarse seguro a bajas concentraciones, pero puede causar irritación en pieles sensibles.","details":"En concentraciones habituales de hasta el 1 %, el fenoxietanol es generalmente bien tolerado, aunque en personas con piel muy reactiva puede provocar enrojecimiento, picor o dermatitis de contacto.
